title: Understanding Torque
text: Torque is the rotational equivalent of linear force. It is calculated as the product of the moment of inertia and the angular acceleration.

title: Moment of Inertia for a Rod
text: The moment of inertia for a rod rotating about its center is given by the formula $$I=(1/12)ml**{2}$$, $$where$$ $$m$$ is the mass and $$l$$ is the length of the rod.

title: Angular Acceleration
text: Angular acceleration can be found using the formula $$\alpha=\frac{\omega_{f}-\omega_{i}}{t}$$, $$where$$ $$\omega_{f}$$ is the final angular velocity, $$\omega_{i}$$ is the initial angular velocity, and $$t$$ is the time taken.

title: Calculate Moment of Inertia
text: Calculate the moment of inertia for the propeller using the formula $$I=(1/12)ml**{2}$$. $$Remember$$ $$to$$ $$consider$$ $$the$$ $$mass$$ $$and$$ $$length$$ $$of$$ $$both$$ $$blades$$.
